topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, student cohorts, and the foundational learning outcomes for cancer biology.

topics.label: Cellular and structural basis of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: They establish that cancer arises through accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal tissue differentiation and three-dimensional architecture, alongside the experimental models used to study these cells.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, malignant progression, and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: They define the clinical and histological distinctions between benign, invasive, and metastatic tumors, illustrate their stepwise progression, and outline standard tumor nomenclature.

topics.label: Cancer morbidity, mortality, and comparative incidence
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the pathological mechanisms causing cancer-related illness and death, and survey the epidemiological incidence of tumors across human populations and diverse animal species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening modalities
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the clinical rationale, histological indicators, and practical effectiveness of screening programs for detecting pre-malignant lesions across different organs.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical preview
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a reminder of the learning outcomes and upcoming practical sessions.
